title: RoboFlow4D: A Lightweight Flow World Model Toward Real-Time Flow-Guided Robotic Manipulation
claim: Prior planners use modular pipelines with 2D or fixed-length flow; ours is end-to-end with adaptive 3D flow, so it is more accurate and faster.
layout: Three stacked pipeline rows (a–c) at top left, results charts at right, task strip at bottom
description: The figure has three parts. The top-left panel stacks three rows that each run left to right: RGB or RGB-D plus text feed into modules, then output a flow visualization. Row (a) is pixel flow with a modular pipeline, and row (b) is fixed-length 3D point flow with a modular pipeline. Both rows have a grumpy emoji. Row (c), in orange and labeled as ours, replaces the module chain with a single RoboFlow4D box and outputs adaptive goal-oriented 3D flow, with a smiling emoji. The top-right panel has bar charts: success rate on LIBERO and ManiSkill3 with +6.2 and +11.0 gains, and latency and parameter bars with 120x faster and -24% callouts. The bottom strip shows four simulated kitchen scenes with rainbow flow trajectories running from a red current-state pin to a gold goal star.
caption: Top left: System-level comparison of various flow-based planning. (a) 2D flow-based planning (Vecerik et al., 2024; Xu et al., 2024) predicts pixel-level flow on images using a modular pipeline with stacked modules, but lacks 3D geometry. (b) Point flow-based frameworks (Li et al., 2025a; Dharmarajan et al., 2025) improve pixel flows by typically predicting fixed temporal-length 3D flows from 3D observations (i.e., RGB-D images), while still relying on a modular pipeline. (c) The end-to-end flow-based pipeline designs a unified world model that directly predicts multiframe flows across time and 3D space (i.e., 4D spacetime) from RGB and text inputs. Bottom: Our RoboFlow4D adaptively adjusts the flow planning horizon from the current state to the atomic task goal. Top right: RoboFlow4D improves the success rate over the base policy by >6.2% in both LIBERO (Liu et al., 2023) and ManiSkill3 (Tao et al., 2024) simulations. Furthermore, RoboFlow4D achieves 120× speedup over modular pipelines and reduces model scale by >24% compared to other flow models.
abstract: Planning and acting in 3D environments is a fundamental capability for robotic manipulation in the real world. Although prior work has explored predictive flow planners to guide 3D manipulation, existing approaches often rely on modular pipelines stacking multiple submodels, resulting in high computational overhead and limited real-time performance. To address these challenges, we introduce RoboFlow4D, a lightweight flow world model that unifies perception and planning by estimating temporal motion in physical 3D space. As an end-to-end framework, RoboFlow4D directly predicts multi-frame 3D flows from visual observations and textual instructions, providing explicit flow-based planning to guide action generation. This design allows seamless integration with general action policies, forming an efficient observation-planning-execution closed loop. Through slow-fast collaboration between flow prediction and action control, RoboFlow4D enables real-time and resource-efficient manipulation. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world settings demonstrate that RoboFlow4D consistently improves manipulation success rates and computational efficiency, advancing flow-guided planning for embodied intelligence.
